fragment: This study presents a comprehensive phylogenomic reassessment of three closely related thermophilic genera within the family Bacillaceae—Anoxybacillus, Geobacillus, and Parageobacillus—using 113 publicly available whole-genome sequences. The primary methodological framework integrated three complementary phylogenomic metrics: a maximum-likelihood core-gene tree derived from 662 orthologous genes, Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI), and Average Amino Acid Identity (AAI) dendrograms. The core gene tree revealed a fundamental phylogenetic split into two main clades: Clade I, containing all Geobacillus, all Parageobacillus, and a subset of Anoxybacillus species; and Clade II, containing the majority of Anoxybacillus species. Clade I was further resolved into three distinct sub-clades corresponding to Geobacillus, Parageobacillus, and a third clade (I-c) composed of Anoxybacillus tepidamans and one unnamed genomospecies. The authors propose that clade I-c be elevated to the new genus Quasigeobacillus gen. nov., supported by 6 unique coding sequence (CDS) identifiers and a position consistently distinct from the three established genera across all three phylogenetic methods. Two Anoxybacillus species (A. vitaminiphilus and A. amylolyticus) showed inconsistent positioning and remain unresolved. The study concludes that taxonomical circumscription based on isolated genus analysis is insufficient; closely related genera must be considered together in phylogenomic workflows to avoid incongruent taxonomic assignments for new strains.

fragment: This study provides two cryo-EM structures of endogenously phosphorylated Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ycf1 (a glutathione transporter of the ABC-C subfamily) at 3.4Å and 4.0Å resolution, capturing previously unobserved ordered states of the intrinsically disordered regulatory R-domain (residues 901-935) in two inward-facing conformations (IFwide and IFnarrow). The R-domain, phosphorylated at S908, T911, and S914, is shown to be helical at its C-terminus (residues 920-929) and forms extensive electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions with NBD1 (spanning three buried hydrophobic sites) and the lasso domain. Biochemical data, including ATPase assays, in-gel phosphoprotein staining, limited proteolysis, and LC-MS/MS, confirm that R-domain phosphorylation reorganizes the Ycf1 architecture and is required for maximal ATPase activity. The dephosphorylated state shows a more complete protease digestion pattern and drastically reduced ATPase activity, consistent with cellular phenotypes where S908 and T911 mutations impair cadmium detoxification. The R-domain encircles NBD1 in both structures, with the IFwide-to-IFnarrow transition involving a rigid body movement of the R-domain/NBD1 complex relative to NBD2 and a reconfiguration of the ATP-binding sites, including partial occlusion of the non-functional ATP site in NBD1. The R-domain phosphorylation sites align with PKA-like (RRAS) and CKII kinase recognition motifs. A conserved inhibitory phosphosite at S251 (lasso domain) is identified in proximity, poised to disrupt the R-domain interaction via electrostatic repulsion. These findings challenge existing models of R-domain disordered-to-ordered transition and provide mechanistic insights for the ABCC transporter family, with clinical relevance to CFTR and lumacaftor binding.

fragment: This study provides two cryo-EM structures of endogenously phosphorylated Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ycf1 (a glutathione transporter of the ABC-C subfamily) at 3.4Å and 4.0Å resolution, capturing previously unobserved ordered states of the intrinsically disordered regulatory R-domain (residues 901-935) in two inward-facing conformations (IFwide and IFnarrow). The R-domain, phosphorylated at S908, T911, and S914, is shown to be helical at its C-terminus (residues 920-929) and forms extensive electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions with NBD1 (spanning three buried hydrophobic sites) and the lasso domain. Biochemical data, including ATPase assays, in-gel phosphoprotein staining, limited proteolysis, and LC-MS/MS, confirm that R-domain phosphorylation reorganizes the Ycf1 architecture and is required for maximal ATPase activity. The dephosphorylated state shows a more complete protease digestion pattern and drastically reduced ATPase activity, consistent with cellular phenotypes where S908 and T911 mutations impair cadmium detoxification. The R-domain encircles NBD1 in both structures, with the IFwide-to-IFnarrow transition involving a rigid body movement of the R-domain/NBD1 complex relative to NBD2 and a reconfiguration of the ATP-binding sites, including partial occlusion of the non-functional ATP site in NBD1. The R-domain phosphorylation sites align with PKA-like (RRAS) and CKII kinase recognition motifs. A conserved inhibitory phosphosite at S251 (lasso domain) is identified in proximity, poised to disrupt the R-domain interaction via electrostatic repulsion. These findings challenge existing models of R-domain disordered-to-ordered transition and provide mechanistic insights for the ABCC transporter family, with clinical relevance to CFTR and lumacaftor binding.

fragment: This study evaluated the interaction between seed treatment with plant growth regulators (PGRs) and nitrogen fertilization on the germination, dry matter yield, and physiological composition of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk. The experiment was conducted in two stages: (1) a germination and initial growth assay (30 DAS) using coated versus conventional seeds with four PGR levels (0, 8, 16, 24 mL·kg⁻¹), and (2) a growth and fertilization experiment with four N application methods. Coated seeds exhibited higher germination percentages and speed index regardless of PGR treatment. A quadratic effect of PGR on germination identified 10.3 mL·kg⁻¹ as the optimal concentration for germination, while 12.8 mL·kg⁻¹ optimized root dry mass. A significant interaction between seed type and PGR level was found for leaf and pseudostem dry mass; coated seeds performed best at 0 and 8.0 mL·kg⁻¹ (optimal at 8.85 and 9.57 mL·kg⁻¹ respectively), while conventional seeds required higher concentrations (15.5 and 18.1 mL·kg⁻¹) for comparable yields. Soil N-fertilization consistently increased dry mass of all plant structures and root volume, with the highest yields achieved when PGR and soil fertilization were combined. Root dry mass increased only under combined PGR and multiple fertilization. Chlorophyll a was significantly increased by PGR, and foliar N-fertilization increased chlorophyll a, b, total chlorophyll, and carotenoids. The study concludes that low-level PGR treatment in coated seeds and soil N-fertilization are effective strategies for enhancing Brachiaria establishment, with PGR acting via hormonal signaling networks and N-fertilization maximizing photosynthetic rates.

A total of 235 consecutive CTO patients undergoing successful DES PCI between November 2004 and October 2010 at Korea University Guro Hospital were divided into long CTO (≥30mm, n=159) and short CTO (<30mm, n=76) groups. The study aimed to determine if lesion length serves as a prognostic factor in the DES era, given prior evidence that long coronary lesions correlate with worse PCI outcomes. Baseline characteristics were similar except for higher prior PCI in the long group and more frequent bifurcation lesions in the short group. In-hospital complications were similar except for more frequent intimal dissection in the long group. At six months, angiographic outcomes, including binary restenosis (19.1% vs. 8.8%, p=0.12) and in-stent restenosis (33.3% vs. 26.6%, p=0.42), showed no statistically significant difference between groups, though a numerical trend toward worse outcomes in long CTO was observed. At two years, hard clinical endpoints—total death (3.1% vs. 5.2%, p=0.43), cardiac death (1.2% vs. 2.6%, p=0.45), MI (1.8% vs. 2.6%, p=0.71), and MACE (21.3% vs. 13.1%, p=0.13)—were statistically similar. However, the long CTO group had significantly higher repeat PCI (18.8% vs. 7.8%, p<0.05) and TVR (16.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified long CTO as a significant independent predictor for repeat PCI (OR 4.26; CI 1.53-11.9; p=0.006) and TVR (OR 4.23; CI 1.52-11.8; p<0.05). The authors conclude that while long CTO lesion length predicts higher revascularization rates, it does not translate into worse hard endpoints in the DES era, and long-term, larger-scale studies are needed to confirm.

fragment:
This paper is a critical rebuttal by King et al. against a bioRxiv preprint by Brüschweiler et al. regarding the mitochondrial ADP/ATP carrier (AAC3) of yeast. Brüschweiler et al. claimed that AAC3 could be refolded from Escherichia coli inclusion bodies to homogeneity in the detergent dodecyl-phosphocholine (DPC) and maintained in a folded, active state for ITC and NMR studies. King et al. systematically refute these claims using thermostability assays, ITC, and functional reconstitution experiments. They demonstrate that DPC, rather than stabilizing AAC3, causes immediate loss of tertiary structure and inactivation upon isolation from the inner mitochondrial membrane. 

Key evidence includes: 1) ITC measurements showing a CATR binding Kd of ~15 μM for DPC-refolded AAC3, versus 72 nM for native AAC3 in dodecyl-maltoside/tetraoleoyl cardiolipin (a 200–2000-fold difference); 2) thermostability assays using CPM fluorescence showing that while mild detergents support a typical protein melt curve, DPC yields no transition, indicating a non-native, unfolded state; 3) functional reconstitution assays where prior dilution into DPC caused complete loss of CATR-sensitive ADP uptake in proteoliposomes. The authors further note that the ADP binding Kd (500 μM) and CATR chemical shift perturbations reported by Brüschweiler et al. are inconsistent with known membrane-bound values and established structural data. They conclude the DPC-refolded AAC3 data lacks biological relevance, as the detergent is harsh enough to denature functional carrier protein.

fragment: This study provides the first evidence that the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum calcium-ATPase (SERCA) regulates paramyxovirus replication of Peste des petits ruminants virus (PPRV) and Newcastle disease virus (NDV). Using a library of chemical inhibitors, Thapsigargin was identified as a SERCA-specific inhibitor that significantly reduces NDV and PPRV replication in Vero cells at a non-cytotoxic concentration of 0.5 µM. Conversely, overexpression of SERCA2 in HeLa/goat kidney cells rescued the inhibitory effect of Thapsigargin, confirming a supportive role for SERCA in viral replication. Time-of-addition and virus step-specific assays revealed that Thapsigargin specifically impairs viral entry and intracellular localization rather than attachment, RNA synthesis, or budding. Immunofluorescence showed that Thapsigargin treatment caused ~70% of cells to exhibit defective cytoplasmic foci of viral proteins instead of surface localization. Notably, NDV acquired significant but incomplete resistance to Thapsigargin on long-term passage (70 passages), with ~100-fold inhibition at P35, while PPRV showed no such resistance. The authors report this as a rare example of a virus acquiring resistance to an inhibitor targeting a cellular host factor, expanding on the precedent set by CVB3/PI4KIIIα and HCV/CsA. The study identifies SERCA as a novel proviral host factor and a candidate drug target for broad-spectrum paramyxovirus antivirals.

fragment: This study characterizes the transcriptional regulation and clinical significance of MicroRNA-196a (MIR196A) in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. MIR196A, transcribed from two genomic loci (HOXC/MIR196A2 and HOXB/MIR196A1), displays complex expression patterns where MIR196A2 expression highly correlates with HOXC genes, particularly HOXC10, in breast tumours but shows more restricted association with HOXC11/10 in normal breast tissue. The authors demonstrate that MIR196A2 is transcriptionally regulated by estrogen via ERα binding to two putative promoter regions (PP1 and PP3) upstream of the transcription start site, with PP1 (the HOXC10 promoter) showing the highest luciferase activity. Long-range transcriptional regulation is mediated by two major interacting elements: a previously identified HOTAIR distal enhancer (HDE) and a novel interacting partner (MIR196A2-Enhancer, mE), both of which physically interact with the MIR196A2/HOXC10 promoter region as confirmed by ChIA-PET and 3C-qPCR. In clinical samples from the METABRIC cohort, high MIR196A expression is significantly over-expressed in breast tumours compared to normal tissue, correlates with increased tumour stage, and serves as a robust prognostic factor: high expression is associated with poor survival in advanced and post-menopausal ER+ disease but better outcome in triple-negative breast cancer. The prognostic impact is state-dependent; in premenopausal women, high MIR196A expression paradoxically associates with good ER+ outcome (one of the few significant biomarkers in this subgroup), whereas in post-menopausal women, high expression predicts poor outcome. Therapeutic resistance further drives MIR196A elevation, with expression significantly increased in tamoxifen-resistant (TAMR) but almost depleted in fulvestrant-resistant (FASR) MCF7 cells, as well as in paclitaxel and adromycin-resistant lines. ERα ChIP-Seq in human patient samples reveals increased ERα occupancy at MIR196A enhancer and promoter regions in non-responders and metastases, suggesting that enhancer over-activation drives therapeutic resistance.

fragment: This study investigates whether conspecific negative density-dependence (CNDD), a proposed mechanism for regulating species coexistence and diversity, operates on seedling establishment of Quercus costaricensis, a monodominant oak in the Talamanca highland forests of Costa Rica. The authors tested the importance of CNDD regulation on seedling survival and recruitment of 3,538 seedlings monitored between 2014 and 2017 at the Cerro de la Muerte Biological Station (3100-3350 m a.s.l.). Using spatial statistics (univariate Ripley's K) and generalized linear mixed-effects models with binomial and quasi-Poisson distributions, they examined the effects of conspecific seedling density, distance to the nearest adult, herbivory intensity, and bamboo (Chusquea spp.) density on annual survival. Contrary to the Janzen-Connell hypothesis, no significant effect of CNDD was found on seedling survival; annual survival remained high (above 63% per year). Instead, herbivory and bamboo density significantly reduced survival. Herbivory paradoxically decreased at higher seedling densities, and seedling survival was highest at intermediate distances from adults, consistent with positive adult facilitation via ectomycorrhizal transfer. In recruitment analyses, seedling recruitment significantly increased with conspecific seedling density but was independent of adult or bamboo density. The authors argue that predator satiation and adult facilitation explain the absence of CNDD, contributing to the species' extreme dominance (>90% of basal stem area) in montane forests. The results challenge the universality of CNDD and suggest that dominant, masting tropical species may escape density-dependent mortality through life-history traits, predator satiation, and mutualistic facilitation.

fragment: This study evaluates the acute toxicity of six engineered nanoparticles (Ag, Au, CuO, ZnO, TiO2, SiO2) and three soluble salts (CuSO4, ZnSO4, AgNO3) on Artemia sp. cysts and hatched nauplii. The authors established two complementary assays: (1) a hatching rate assay where hydrated cysts were exposed to nanoparticles at 100 mg/L and 10 mg/L in 25% salt water, measuring hatching rate (fully hatched motile nauplii/total cysts) after 24 hours, and (2) a standard Artemia toxicity test (ARC protocol) where 10 normally hatched nauplii were exposed to concentrations ranging from 0.01 to 100 mg/L, measuring mortality over 48 hours. Physicochemical characterization via TEM and DLS revealed that nanoparticles exhibited reduced size and altered dispersion behavior in salt water compared to MilliQ water, with visible flocculation for CuO and ZnO. Key results showed that Ag and CuO NPs were the most toxic; Ag NPs at 100 mg/L reduced hatching to ~29% with only 50% viability, and in the larval test, the LC50 of Ag NPs was ~10.12 mg/L at 24 hours. The study established a toxicity order of Ag > CuO > ZnO > Au > TiO2 > SiO2. A strong inverse correlation (r = -0.7853) was found between hatching rate reduction and larval mortality, suggesting that hatching rate can serve as a valid surrogate endpoint. Oxidative stress was confirmed via DCFDA staining, showing ROS accumulation primarily in Ag-exposed nauplii and their guts. The study concludes that Artemia sp. are a robust, cost-effective model for high-throughput nanoparticle hazard identification, with hatching tests providing an efficient pre-screening alternative to standard lethality assays.
